instructions:
# Batch Requests

## What this skill does

Designs and tests batch APIs: JSON-RPC batch arrays, GraphQL multi-operation/alias batching, and dedicated /batch endpoints with per-request paths.

## When to use

- Clients make many small calls that can be grouped
- Reducing round trips over high-latency networks
- Bulk reads or writes in one operation

## Real commands

```bash
# JSON-RPC batch
curl -X POST http://localhost:8545 -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"eth_blockNumber","id":1},{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"eth_chainId","id":2}]'

# GraphQL batch (JSON array of operations)
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/graphql -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '[{"query":"{users{id}}"},{"query":"{posts{id}}"}]'

# Dedicated batch endpoint
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/batch -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"requests":[{"path":"/users/1","method":"GET"},{"path":"/posts","method":"GET"}]}'
```

## Testing

- Compare time_total for N single calls vs one batch call
- Assert per-item status codes in the batch response

## Best practices

- Cap batch sizes to bound server work (e.g. 100 items)
- Return per-item errors, not all-or-nothing
- Use id/alias mapping so clients can correlate responses
- Batch only idempotent or cache-friendly reads by default

examples.input: Reduce round trips for our dashboard widgets
examples.output: Implements a /batch endpoint accepting requests array, and shows curl comparisons of latency between sequential and batched calls.

examples.input: Batch two GraphQL queries into one request
examples.output: Shows the JSON-array batch form and the single-document aliased form, and compares responses.
